intro.label: When it stops something
intro.title: When yokoten stops a command
intro.body: yokoten stops a command before it runs, and prints why. Nothing was done, so there is nothing to undo. This is a real stop:

read.title: How to read a stop
read.body: Every stop has the same four parts:
parts: The command, what it would do, and the rule's name in brackets.
The safe way to do it, or who must do it.

tell.title: What to tell your agent
tell.body: Usually nothing. Your agent reads the same lines and takes the Instead route on its own.
tell.only: When the Instead line says only you can do it, such as a release, the agent stops and leaves it to you. Do that step yourself, when you are ready.

protects.title: What it protects
protects.body: yokoten protects five things. All five are on in every project after `npx yokoten`, with nothing to set.

items.title: Your work
items.body: a force push, a hard reset, deleting `.git`, and other ways to lose work.

items.title: Your secrets
items.body: a commit that adds a key, a private email or an IP address.

items.title: Your releases
items.body: a new tag, a package publish, or making a repo public. Only you decide when to release.

items.title: The code you run
items.body: a download that a program would run before anyone reads it.

items.title: The guard itself
items.body: skipping the commit check, or switching it off.

wrong.title: If a stop looks wrong
wrong.body: Open an issue on GitHub and paste the line that starts with `yokoten stopped this:`. Leave out keys, emails and server names.
